title: Intervene on state, prompt and evaluator separately
advisorGate: B2 independently accepted; B3 selected as final production round
question: When self-reports match observationally, which crossed interventions distinguish functional state access from prompt following, and which judgments remain evaluator effects?
model: Exact binary factorial channels Z,P,R,F,E,V. Observational P=Z; crossed P and Z independent. One scripted R channel reads Z and another reads P, both with .9 accuracy to their input. F follows prompt framing; E independently cues a scripted evaluator V. No variable represents phenomenal consciousness.
incomingEvidence: B2 showed that selecting an interpretation on discovery does not establish a held-out relationship. B3 freezes the report/evaluator map and uses crossed interventions to distinguish a known functional causal mechanism from matched observational reports.
controls: Prompt-only reporter with identical observational performance
Known .9 state-access channel as positive functional control
limits: Zero live model calls and zero human observations.
Z is a scripted computational bit, not a consciousness measurement; no phenomenal ground-truth labels are assigned.
F, E and V are scripted affirmation/evaluator channels, not observed human or AI reports or judgments.
All channel probabilities are stipulated for identification, not fitted to biological or AI data.
A known functional state-readout mechanism is distinguishable here only because intervention and channel assumptions are supplied.
The toy model neither estimates an AI consciousness probability nor replicates the primary introspection study.
No known target access, self-report or theory indicator identifies a higher consciousness source in this model.
